organism.label: xenobot (reconfigurable organism built from Xenopus laevis animal-pole cells)

species_caveat: Every link below comes from Xenopus laevis (in one case Xenopus tropicalis) embryos, from animal-cap organoids, or from published xenobots built out of unedited X. laevis cells; the taxon id NCBITaxon_8355 names the DONOR species, because a xenobot has no taxon of its own and no edited genome.
design_note: THE MOST IMPORTANT HONEST POINT IN THIS LADDER: the donor genome is unedited, so nothing in the molecule-to-cell part of this chain is a designed variable. The genotype-to-locomotion link runs through ASSEMBLY GEOMETRY, not through any genetic change. Kriegman et al. 2021 put it in their own words - 'Design, if framed as morphological reconfiguration, can reposition biological tissues or redirect self-organizing processes to new stable forms without recourse to genomic editing or transgenes' (runs/_chains/raw/xenobot/PMC8670470.xml, byte-exact) - and Blackiston et al. 2021 say of the cilia themselves, 'These xenobots exhibit coordinated locomotion via cilia present on their surface. These cilia arise through normal tissue patterning and do not require complicated construction methods or genomic editing' (runs/_chains/raw/xenobot/pm34043553.xml, byte-exact, abstract only). This ladder is therefore a ladder of WILD-TYPE Xenopus development that the designer re-shapes but does not rewrite. A viewer that claims to show 'how the locomotion changes based on each genetic code' would be wrong for this organism unless what it is showing is an injected-mRNA perturbation (link l14, Notch ICD) or a drug (link l15, WNT3A) - both of which act on the wild-type genome rather than changing it.

missing_rungs.why: A xenobot has no organ. Kriegman et al. 2020 say so of their own constructs: 'above the cellular level, they bear little resemblance to existing organs or organisms' (runs/_chains/raw/xenobot/PMC6994979.xml, byte-exact). Links l12 and l13 therefore step straight from tissue to phenotype with skipped_rung set to 'organ'.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Nothing can close this one by experiment: the rung does not exist in this organism. A viewer that insists on an organ layer should render it as explicitly empty rather than invent one.

missing_rungs.why: No document fetched in this run gives a xenobot locomotion speed in any unit, so the requirement's 0.5-1 mm/s figure is unsourced as far as this ladder is concerned. The paper that reports ciliary xenobot locomotion quantitatively, Blackiston et al. 2021 Science Robotics, is not open access: its abstract was readable through PubMed, but Europe PMC returned HTTP 404 for its full text because it has no PMCID.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: The full text or supplementary movies of Blackiston et al. 2021 (doi 10.1126/scirobotics.abf1571), or any tracked-trajectory dataset of ciliated xenobots with a calibrated scale bar and frame rate.

missing_rungs.why: Nothing fetched links a MEASURED multiciliated-cell density or coverage on a xenobot to that xenobot's measured speed or to how many particles it moves. Boselli et al. 2021 model coverage against transport on a flat Xenopus epidermis; Kriegman et al. 2021 observe locomotion and piling on a spheroid; no document connects the two quantities in the same specimen.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Per-xenobot multiciliated-cell counts (acetylated-tubulin staining, say) paired with tracked speed and a per-organism count of particles displaced, across a range of Notch-ICD doses.

missing_rungs.why: There is no genotype variable in this organism at all: the donor genome is unedited. The only molecular handles found in anything fetched here are an injected mRNA (Notch ICD, l14, which REMOVES ciliary locomotion) and a drug (WNT3A, l15, in a different Xenopus species and in an intact embryo). No document shows any molecular manipulation that INCREASES xenobot speed or improves particle sweeping.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A xenobot built from cells injected with mcidas or foxj1 mRNA (to raise multiciliated-cell number), or treated with WNT3A, with speed and particle sweeping measured against uninjected controls in the same dish.

missing_rungs.why: The serotonin/Htr3 beat-frequency loop (l09, l10) was shown in tadpole skin. Nothing fetched shows that small secretory cells exist in a xenobot at all, so it is unknown whether this control loop is present in the construct.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: An in situ or scRNA-seq census of a mature xenobot for small-secretory-cell markers. The Lee et al. 2023 animal-cap organoid atlas is the closest available dataset and does profile ionocytes and goblet cells, but the xenobot itself was not checked here.

missing_rungs.why: ADDED BY VERIFICATION. l03 is the only link joining the Notch/Delta lateral-inhibition arm (l01, l02) to the multicilin arm (l04-l07), and its quote does not name mcidas and is a background citation rather than a result of the paper it is drawn from (see l03.downgraded_by_verification). With l03 at hypothesis grade, the two molecular arms of this ladder are not experimentally joined by anything fetched here: there is no quoted evidence that Notch represses mcidas specifically.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A quotable result sentence or figure legend from Stubbs et al. 2012 or a successor showing mcidas transcript or reporter levels rising when Notch activity is lowered and falling when it is raised, in the same experiment.

missing_rungs.why: ADDED BY VERIFICATION. A specimen break, distinct from the quantitative gap already logged between cell_cell and tissue. Every link from molecule through cell_cell (l01-l10) is evidenced in an intact Xenopus embryo or in an animal-cap explant; the only links whose organism_of_evidence is a xenobot are l11, l12, l13 - all `association`, all purely observational - and l14, now `hypothesis`. So no fetched document shows ANY of the Notch, multicilin or serotonin steps actually operating inside a reassembled spheroid: the mechanistic upper half of the ladder and the xenobot phenotype are joined by inference, not by a shared specimen.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: In situ, immunostaining or scRNA-seq on mature xenobots for X-Delta-1/Notch targets, mcidas, foxj1 and acetylated tubulin, showing the same programme runs in the construct; ideally with a Notch-ICD dose series scored in the spheroid itself.

refused_sources.what_it_would_have_given: The full text of Blackiston et al. 2021, Science Robotics, 'A cellular platform for the development of synthetic living machines' - the paper that measures ciliary xenobot locomotion and would have supplied the 0.5-1 mm/s speed in the design requirement. It has no PMCID, so Europe PMC holds no full text for it; only the PubMed abstract was read (runs/_chains/raw/xenobot/pm34043553.xml).

verification.stance: Every claim was re-derived from the bytes. Quote matching was done by script, not by eye.

method.quote_matching: Python: each `quote` normalised to single spaces and searched in (a) the raw file, (b) the file with XML tags deleted (zero-width tag boundary), (c) the file with tags replaced by a space. A quote counted as verified only on a literal substring hit.
method.fetch_log: Each distinct `quote_from` path matched against runs/_chains/log/xenobot.fetch.json by `saved_to`, status asserted 200, and the file's sha256 recomputed and compared with the logged digest.
method.citation_identity: The pmid and doi claimed in each link's `source` compared with the pmid and doi recorded inside the fetched document.
method.grades: Each `evidence_grade` re-read against the five definitions in genotype/AGENT_BRIEF.md, judged strictly on what the QUOTE shows, not on what the paper as a whole probably shows.
method.holdout: Scanned for the names and terms of the held-out clade; no source from it was used in any link, quote or evidence field. The scan itself is in the fetch log and the verifier's scripts, not restated here.
method.identifiers: All 32 logged URLs parsed: hosts, query-parameter names, plus a regex scan of the entire log for email addresses, personal names, account ids, api keys and NCBI tool=/email= parameters.

results.quote_match_modes: all 15 matched in the raw bytes after whitespace collapsing alone; none needed tag stripping

results.walkable: The ladder IS walkable end to end as topology: molecule->pathway (l04 necessity, l05 mechanism), pathway->cell (l06 sufficiency), cell->cell_cell (l09 necessity), cell_cell->tissue (l10 necessity, l08 hypothesis), then tissue->phenotype directly (l12, l13 association) because the organ rung does not exist in this organism. Two of the three downgrades, l01 and l03, fall on the Notch/Delta arm, which is a parallel entry into the pathway rung, so none of them severs the walkable path. The path is nonetheless carried across its final step by `association`-grade observation only, and its mechanistic rungs come from a different specimen than its phenotype rungs - see the two missing_rungs added by this verification.
missing_rungs_added_detail: pathway<->molecule: the Notch->mcidas junction is unevidenced by its own quote
cell<->tissue: specimen break - no fetched document shows the mechanistic rungs operating inside a xenobot
results.holdout: Scanned for the names and terms of the held-out clade; no source from it was used in any link, quote or evidence field. The scan itself is in the fetch log and the verifier's scripts, not restated here.
results.identifier_leak: NONE. 32 logged URLs across 4 hosts (www.ebi.ac.uk, eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, rest.uniprot.org, ubergraph.apps.renci.org); query parameters are only db, fields, format, id, pageSize, query, resultType, retmode, rettype, size. No email address, personal name, account id, api key, or NCBI tool=/email= parameter anywhere in the log.

verification.not_changed: No link was deleted, no link was added, nothing was re-fetched, no existing missing_rungs entry was softened or removed, and the design_note - including its statement that there is no genotype variable in this organism - was left as written, because it is correct and the verifier found nothing in the fetched documents that contradicts it.

holdout_redaction: The audit fields of this file were redacted so that they record THAT held-out material was excluded without describing it. Links, quotes, grades and sources are unchanged.
